item.title: China, EU hold 17th economic, financial dialogue in Beijing
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-24
China, EU hold 17th economic, financial dialogue in Beijing BEIJING, Nov. 23 (Xinhua) -- The 17th China-EU Economic and Financial Dialogue was held in Beijing on Monday, with both sides discussing macroeconomic conditions and policies, as well as China-EU multilateral cooperation within the G20. China's Vice Minister of Finance Liao Min, who co-chaired the dialogue, said that under the current circumstances, China and the EU should jointly uphold and practice true multilateralism and work toward an open world economy to inject greater stability and certainty into the global economy. Major economies, including China and the EU, should take necessary measures to advance structural reforms, deepen macroeconomic policy coordination, keep global industrial and supply chains stable and smooth, and promote global economic and financial stability, Liao said. China is ready to expand mutual openness with the EU and make the cooperation pie bigger, Liao added, calling on the EU side to respect market economy principles and fair competition, and provide a fair, just and non-discriminatory business environment for Chinese enterprises. Noting that the China-EU Economic and Financial Dialogue is an important platform for the two sides to deepen macroeconomic policy coordination and strengthen financial and economic cooperation, the EU side said it values macroeconomic policy communication and practical cooperation with China. The EU side said it is willing to strengthen constructive dialogue with China on the basis of mutual respect and reciprocal openness, carry out equal and mutually beneficial cooperation, properly address differences and disagreements, and advance the rebalancing of EU-China economic relations in an orderly manner. item.title: Power use surges in China's EV charging, data service sectors in October
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-24
Power use surges in China's EV charging, data service sectors in October BEIJING, Nov. 23 (Xinhua) -- Electricity consumption by China's electric vehicle charging and internet data service sectors soared in October, highlighting robust demand from the country's fast-growing new-energy vehicle and digital industries, official data showed Monday. Power consumption by charging and battery-swapping services reached 18.6 billion kilowatt-hours in October, surging 59.4 percent year on year, while that of internet data services jumped 34.7 percent to 9.9 billion kilowatt-hours, according to the National Energy Administration. NEVs accounted for 64.3 percent of new car sales last month, up from 61.6 percent in September, while the cumulative share for the first 10 months climbed to 54.8 percent, according to the China Association of Automobile Manufacturers. China's total electricity consumption for October stood at 870.9 billion kilowatt-hours, an increase of 1.6 percent year on year. Driven by rapid growth in electricity consumption by new business forms, power use in the tertiary industry grew the fastest among all industries, said Wu Liqiang, an official with the China Electricity Council. Electricity consumption by the tertiary industry rose 6.3 percent year on year to 171.4 billion kilowatt-hours in October. Electricity consumption by the primary industry stood at 12.4 billion kilowatt-hours, up 3.3 percent year on year, while power use by the secondary industry edged up 1.8 percent to 579 billion kilowatt-hours. Notably, power consumption by high-tech and equipment manufacturing industries climbed 6.5 percent year on year to 111.1 billion kilowatt-hours in October. In October, power use in high energy-consuming manufacturing sector posted negative year-on-year growth for three consecutive months, said Wu. In the first 10 months of 2026, China's total electricity consumption rose 3.7 percent year on year to 8.94 trillion kilowatt-hours. Electricity use by charging and battery-swapping services surged 55.9 percent in this period, while that of internet data services increased by 40.8 percent. According to an annual development report on China's electric power industry released by the China Electricity Council in July, total electricity consumption nationwide in 2026 is expected to increase by 5 percent to 6 percent year on year. item.title: Why is Europe's tech spotlight brightening with Chinese innovations?
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-24
Why is Europe's tech spotlight brightening with Chinese innovations? Chinese humanoid robots perform at Web Summit 2026 in Lisbon, Portugal. (Photo/websummit.com) At Web Summit 2026 recently held in Lisbon, Portugal, performances by humanoid robots from China stole the spotlight. Clips quickly gained traction on social media, giving overseas netizens a closer look at the appeal of Chinese technology. At the opening ceremony, Web Summit CEO and founder Paddy Cosgrave said that future technology superstars would increasingly come from China. At a premier global tech gathering hosted in Europe, why did Chinese tech elements keep standing out, and why was China's presence growing more prominent? China's strong innovation capabilities are the most direct explanation. Chinese companies including Tencent, Xiaomi, Unitree Robotics, and Pony.ai, participated in this year's summit, showcasing breakthroughs across frontier fields such as artificial intelligence (AI), embodied AI, and autonomous driving. At the event, which brought together roughly 70,000 technology professionals, entrepreneurs and investors from around the world, Chinese innovations captured the attention of global industry players, thanks to solid technological foundations and competitive products. The growing attention to Chinese innovation also reflects a subtle shift in the global innovation landscape. This year's opening ceremony featured a dedicated frontier technology showcase. Chinese companies were invited to present solutions such as humanoid robots and flying cars, painting a picture of everyday life in the future for European audiences. Staff members collect data in a range of scenarios at an embodied AI robot data collection and training center in Suqian, east China's Jiangsu province. (Photo/Wang Shuaifu) For years, Silicon Valley and Europe's established research hubs were synonymous with global innovation centers. Today, when Europe looks for a tangible glimpse of tomorrow, its gaze is turning proactively toward China. That marks a shift in how the international community views China's role in innovation. Looking deeper, the rising prominence of Chinese innovations in Europe reflects not only shared needs, but also the inevitable logic of industrial development. Europe is home to many top universities and long-standing prowess in basic research and high-end manufacturing, yet faces bottlenecks in commercializing innovation. These include an underdeveloped digital platform ecosystem, limited cloud computing capacity, and slower AI commercialization. Bridging the "last mile" from lab breakthroughs to market application remains a persistent challenge for European industry. China's innovation drive has charted a differentiated path. By leveraging a massive engineering workforce, a complete industrial chain, and vast application scenarios, new technologies can rapidly complete a closed-loop iteration from laboratory to production line to real-world applications. Robots do more than perform on stage. They help in warehouses and retail stores. AI goes beyond conversations. It cuts costs and raises efficiency in industrial settings. What truly resonates in Europe is the substantial application potential and win-win business opportunities behind these innovations. Still, discordant voices persist. Even as growing numbers of business leaders and researchers recognize China as an indispensable force on the global innovation landscape, some European politicians remain conflicted about Chinese technology. They repeatedly hype the "de-risking" narrative and erect barriers in an attempt to restrict China-Europe cooperation on the sci-tech front. Yet such moves have neither changed the stance of the business and tech communities nor halted the endogenous drive for bilateral cooperation. Sci-tech cooperation between China and Europe is inherently built on complementary strengths. Europe's basic research and talent pool complement China's engineering capabilities and application testing. They are closely aligned in such fields as AI, green technology, and smart manufacturing. Foreign visitors watch a performance by a humanoid robot and a quadruped robot dog at a direct-operated store of Unitree Robotics on Wangfujing pedestrian street in Beijing. (Photo/Guo Junfeng) European enterprises can draw on Chinese solutions to accelerate digital transformation, while Chinese innovation entities can leverage European resources to enhance their technologies. This model of mutual empowerment has a solid foundation and enjoys broad room to grow. Sci-tech innovation is not a zero-sum game, and pursuing technological self-reliance is by no means synonymous with self-isolation. Choosing diverse technology supply and broad collaborative networks gives industrial development greater resilience. Equating competition with a threat or dismissing pragmatic cooperation as dependence only limits oneself and hinders future growth. When Europe's tech community looks toward China, it sees not only today's technological achievements, but a future of cooperation. Copyright © 2026 People's Daily Online. All Rights Reserved.

item.title: Decoding Shenzhen: the city that wowed APEC leaders
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-24
Decoding Shenzhen: the city that wowed APEC leaders SHENZHEN, Nov. 23 (Xinhua) -- The 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting has just wrapped up in China's Shenzhen, and the leaders did not leave the host city without a comment. On various occasions, they praised the city's futuristic vibe and meteoric rise. This photo taken on Nov. 5, 2026 shows an APEC-themed installation in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province. (Xinhua/Liang Xu) During his stay in Shenzhen, Russian President Vladimir Putin called the southern Chinese city in Guangdong Province "impressive," hailing it as one of the world's most advanced and dynamic metropolises. He noted that the city organically combines a high level of urbanization, a comfortable urban environment and an innovative production base. As one of the key investment centers in the Asia-Pacific, Shenzhen reflects the profound technological, economic and social transformations taking place in China and across Asia, Putin said. U.S. President Donald Trump, back in Washington after his APEC trip, spoke highly of Shenzhen at a White House press conference. "When you were there, you could see it. It was amazing energy," he said, adding that the city is clean and immaculate, and it has been built in a short period of time. Recalling his first visit to Shenzhen in 1998, Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese described the city as an example of the Asia-Pacific region's extraordinary rise. "If you had put two photos together, 1998 and 2026, you would not think it was the same place," the prime minister said. China's achievement "is worth celebrating and should certainly not be taken for granted," he added. A drone photo taken on Oct. 23, 2026 shows a view of Shenzhen Bay Park in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province. (Xinhua/Mao Siqian) Shenzhen is often seen as the epitome of China's development over more than four decades. It has risen from a small fishing village to the window of China's reform and opening up, and then to an innovation hub and home to tech giants such as Huawei, BYD, Tencent and DJI. Even before hosting the APEC event, Shenzhen had already become one of China's top spots for international tourists, while drawing global media spotlight for its rapid growth and technological prowess. ENGINE OF INNOVATION When Shenzhen, adjacent to Hong Kong, was designated a special economic zone in 1980, it was a border town of just over 300,000 people, its roads narrow and its industrial base virtually nonexistent. Today, it is a megacity of more than 18 million residents, its skyline dense with high-rises and its streets thick with traffic. In 2025, Shenzhen's GDP soared to 3.87 trillion yuan (about 576.58 billion U.S. dollars), 14,000 times its GDP in 1980, a pace rare in the history of global urbanization. "Shenzhen's success offers many lessons. In many ways, it is China's own success story in miniature," said Ameen Muneer Mohammed Al-Obaidi, a reporter with China Arab TV. More recently, the city has evolved from a world factory into an innovation and advanced manufacturing hub with vibrant industry clusters spanning sectors from new energy to artificial intelligence (AI). This photo taken on May 6, 2026 shows a drone delivering takeout food in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province. (Xinhua/Mao Siqian) Drones zip across city blocks, streets buzz with electric vehicles, and an AI industry booms -- this is the Shenzhen that President of the Republic of Korea Lee Jae Myung saw during the APEC meeting. The city serves as a vivid testament to how future technologies can transform our lives, and technologies once considered part of the distant future have already become part of daily life here, Lee said. Experts have accredited Shenzhen's leading position in multiple technological fronts to the city's heavy investment in research and development (R&D). Data shows that in 2025, Shenzhen's total R&D investment reached 245.31 billion yuan, or 6.67 percent of its GDP, with enterprises accounting for more than 93 percent of total R&D investment. The city also draws strength from the manufacturing prowess in the Pearl River Delta and integrated growth in the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area. The Shenzhen-Zhongshan Link, a major cross-sea transportation project that opened to traffic in 2024, has prompted Shenzhen companies to set up factories in cities like Zhongshan to benefit from their manufacturing capacity and larger industrial space. Tourists from Jamaica interact with a humanoid robot at a robot shop in Longgang District of Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province, Aug. 4, 2026. (Xinhua/Liang Xu) At Huaqiangbei, Shenzhen's mega electronics marketplace, a design can be sketched in the morning, turned into a prototype by afternoon, mass-produced the next day, and shipped overseas within a week. About 3 million parcels leave the area every day. Huaqiangbei welcomed nearly 8,000 foreign buyers on an average day this year, according to local government. Janwick Hattingh, from South Africa, bought a power bank there. "It's quite advanced here," he said. "You can find any tech product you can think of." MODEL OF COOPERATION Addressing the APEC CEO Summit, held on Nov. 17-18 on the sidelines of the APEC meeting, Thai Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul named Shenzhen the best-fitting place for Asia-Pacific economies to discuss how to adapt to a changing world and build a more prosperous future together. The city, he said, shows what transformation can achieve when an economy opens itself to the world. Openness is in Shenzhen's DNA. For more than four decades, Shenzhen has kept opening wider to the world. In the first 10 months of this year, its imports and exports reached 5.25 trillion yuan, up 40.9 percent year on year. Workers operate at a cherry packing plant in Santiago, Chile, Oct. 29, 2026. (Xinhua/Zhou Jiayi) During the Shenzhen meeting, Chilean President Jose Antonio Kast and his wife visited a local fruit shop to celebrate the arrival in China of new-season Chilean cherries and invited Chinese consumers to taste them. The timing was no accident. China is currently the largest export destination for Chilean cherries. Kast noted that Chile will expand the scale of trade and investment cooperation with China, broaden collaboration in agriculture, mining, new energy vehicles, infrastructure development and AI, and promote exchanges in education and culture. Cherries are just one part of a much larger flow in Asia-Pacific cooperation. Shenzhen's trade with other APEC economies has grown more than tenfold in nearly three decades, surging from 267.5 billion yuan in 1996 to 3.13 trillion yuan in 2025. Multinational companies are placing not only R&D centers and regional headquarters in Shenzhen, but also their long-term strategic commitments. Apple has set up an applied research lab in the city, while DHL Express has put its Shenzhen super gateway into operation, its largest single investment project in the Chinese mainland to date. Cooperation between Shenzhen and other APEC economies is shifting from "bringing in" to "creating together." An aerial drone photo taken on Oct. 20, 2026 shows a cargo ship sailing toward Yantian Port in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province. (Xinhua) Teo Siong Seng, executive chairman of Pacific International Lines in Singapore, noted that six of the world's ten largest container ports, including Shenzhen, are in China. He expressed hope that APEC will further expand regional connectivity and make the connections among its members more resilient and sustainable. "As the Chinese proverb reminds us, 'hai na bai chuan,' which means the sea is vast because it embraces the waters of many rivers," said Kristalina Georgieva, managing director of the International Monetary Fund. "When we pull together, what comes into view is shared prosperity and peace." (Reporting by Cui Enhui, Wang Jian, Yao Yuan, Wang Pan and Sun Fe) Copyright © 2026 People's Daily Online. All Rights Reserved.

item.title: China unveils Shenzhou-24 crew for space station mission, including first foreign astronaut
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-24
China unveils Shenzhou-24 crew for space station mission, including first foreign astronaut This undated photo shows Shenzhou-24 crew members Tang Hongbo (C), Wu Yi (R), and Pakistani astronaut Muhammad Zeeshan Ali. Chinese astronauts Tang Hongbo, Wu Yi, and Pakistani astronaut Muhammad Zeeshan Ali will carry out the Shenzhou-24 crewed spaceflight mission, the China Manned Space Agency announced on Tuesday. (Xinhua) JIUQUAN, Nov. 24 (Xinhua) -- Chinese astronauts Tang Hongbo, Wu Yi, and Pakistani astronaut Muhammad Zeeshan Ali will carry out the Shenzhou-24 crewed spaceflight mission, with Tang serving as commander, the China Manned Space Agency announced on Tuesday. The three astronauts are a spacecraft pilot, a flight engineer and a payload specialist, respectively. Tang has participated in the Shenzhou-12 and Shenzhou-17 crewed flight missions and is about to become the first astronaut to visit China's Tiangong space station three times. Wu comes from the country's third batch of astronauts and will embark on his first spaceflight mission. Ali will become the first foreign astronaut to visit Tiangong. China's Shenzhou-24 crewed spaceship is scheduled to be launched at 8:18 a.m. (Beijing Time) Wednesday from the Jiuquan Satellite Launch Center in northwest China, Zhang Jingbo, spokesperson of the agency, said at a press conference. item.title: Xi extends congratulations on Int'l Day of Solidarity with Palestinian People
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-24
Xi extends congratulations on Int'l Day of Solidarity with Palestinian People BEIJING, Nov. 24 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping extended congratulations to a UN meeting held on Monday to commemorate the International Day of Solidarity with the Palestinian People. In his message, Xi said that the Palestinian question lies at the heart of the Middle East issue, adding that the current tensions in the Middle East should not divert the international community's attention from the Palestinian issue. The key to resolving the Palestinian question is to stay on course toward the two-state solution and promote the resumption of peace talks between Palestine and Israel, Xi said. He stressed that the governance of the West Bank and post-war reconstruction in Gaza should be advanced in accordance with the principle of "Palestinians governing Palestine," and opposed any land-grabbing or rights-infringing actions targeting the Palestinian people. The international community should translate its consensus and commitments in support of Palestine into concrete actions, promote a lasting ceasefire in Gaza and protect the safety of civilians, Xi said. Xi said that justice will prevail and must not be absent. China has always firmly supported the just cause of the Palestinian people to restore their legitimate national rights, he said. China will continue to work with all countries that cherish peace and uphold justice to promote the early realization of a comprehensive, just and lasting solution of the Palestinian question, based on the rule of international law and with a view to addressing both its symptoms and root causes, Xi said. Such efforts will contribute to lasting peace and stability in the Middle East and make positive contributions to world peace, stability, development and prosperity, Xi added.
